tax.text: He voted against a budget that paired tax cuts for wealthy people and corporations with cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.
tax.quote: This budget is all about giving massive tax cuts to billionaires and big corporations while gutting the vital services that everyday Americans, seniors, and Veterans rely on.

wages.text: Carbajal’s Affordability Agenda proposes increasing the minimum wage and strengthening workers’ role in workplace decisions.
wages.quote: Increase the minimum wage and ensure workers have a seat at the table.

trade.text: Carbajal called for reversing blanket tariffs and restoring free trade, while saying tariffs may be effective in limited, short-term circumstances.
trade.quote: I urge you to restore free trade before small businesses suffer irreparable harm and American families face lasting financial strain.

debt.text: Carbajal opposes privatizing Social Security and converting Medicare to vouchers.
debt.quote: I strongly oppose privatizing Social Security and oppose turning Medicare into a voucher system.

housing.text: Carbajal co-led legislation to incentivize construction of more housing and supported a plan to build four million homes over the next decade.
housing.quote: Cut red tape and update permitting and zoning to build four million homes in the next decade.

immigration.text: Carbajal co-led and sponsored legislation providing legal status, immigration protections, and pathways to citizenship for some undocumented immigrants.
immigration.quote: The bill includes commonsense reforms to legal status and protections for undocumented immigrants, border security investments, and improved asylum and visa processes.

guns.text: Carbajal supports universal background checks and an assault-weapons ban.
guns.quote: Congress must also pass universal background checks, a policy supported by nearly 90 percent of the American people

abortion.text: Carbajal cosponsored legislation protecting abortion access nationwide.
abortion.quote: That’s why I am a co-sponsor and leading advocate for the Women’s Health Protection Act, which would explicitly protect the right to an abortion nationwide.

cannabis.text: Carbajal voted to federally decriminalize marijuana.
cannabis.quote: The MORE Act is a long overdue measure which decriminalizes marijuana at the federal level

health.text: Carbajal’s Affordability Agenda proposes expanding Medicaid access and strengthening Medicare’s guaranteed benefits.
health.quote: Expand access to care by fully funding Medicaid and strengthening Medicare’s guaranteed benefits.

energy.text: Carbajal called for restoring federal authority to regulate greenhouse-gas pollution and reversing the administration’s rollback of environmental protections.
energy.quote: The Administration has a responsibility to protect the American people from the escalating dangers of climate change, and I call on them to reverse this decision immediately.

voting.text: Carbajal voted for automatic and same-day voter registration.
voting.quote: Expanding automatic voter registration and same day registration.

tax.text: Smith said higher earners should contribute appropriately while also supporting tax relief and lower costs for working families.
tax.quote: Those who do well should contribute appropriately, but the bigger issue is ensuring everyone plays by the same rules.

debt.text: Smith strongly supports cutting federal spending and eliminating waste to reduce the national debt.
debt.quote: We must get federal spending under control to address our growing national debt.

housing.text: Smith supports expanding the housing supply, including starter homes, townhomes and family housing, while reducing unnecessary construction regulations.
housing.quote: I will fight to expand the housing supply in areas that make sense, including starter homes, townhomes and family housing

immigration.text: Smith pairs support for strong border security and removing offenders with legal clarity for long-term residents.
immigration.quote: The United States should welcome immigrants who follow the law, contribute to our economy, and respect our Constitution.

guns.text: Smith supports restrictions targeting violent felons, domestic abusers and people found dangerous by a court, but opposes broad new restrictions on law-abiding gun owners.
guns.quote: I do not support broad new restrictions on law-abiding citizens.

abortion.text: Smith said he supports legal access to abortion and that the government should not decide.
abortion.quote: I support access to abortion and believe these decisions should be made by women and their doctors, not the federal government.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Smith says athletic policies should be based on biological differences while providing accommodations that respect individual dignity.
gender.quote: Policies should be based on biological differences in athletics and provide appropriate accommodations that respect everyone’s dignity.

energy.text: Smith prioritizes lowering household energy costs while also supporting a mix of reliable baseload power and clean generation.
energy.quote: Cut wasteful spending, lower the cost of housing, energy, and food, and expand homeownership for working families.

voting.text: Smith said requiring voter identification is a reasonable measure to protect election integrity.
voting.quote: Requiring identification to vote is a reasonable step to protect election integrity and maintain public trust.
